2024 Chevrolet Camaro SS Convertible Comes Up for Sale With 4k Miles and a Single Owner From New
76 photos
Photo: Motorcar Classics
New York-based Motorcar Classics probably thinks it has you covered if you're willing to write a rather small check for this 2024 Chevrolet Camaro SS that also has sensible looks, few miles on the odometer, and just one owner since new.
The mid-size General Motors sports car was born for the 1967 model year to compete in the newly established pony car subsegment alongside its platform sibling, the Pontiac Firebird, in a bid to steal the spotlight from the ultra-popular Ford Mustang. Initially, four generations were created, all with their own life stories, before production originally ended in 2002.
However, the fever of retro-modern American sports cars was just hitting with the S197 fifth-generation Ford Mustang launched for the 2005 model year, and General Motors had no choice but to follow in the footsteps of the third-generation 2008 Dodge Challenger, reintroducing the Camaro as a complete redesign on a brand-new platform for the 2010 model year.
The fifth and sixth generations were akin to the newer Ford Mustang, as they slowly transitioned to a more traditional sports car allure, while the Dodge Challenger remained steadfast in its retro looks, which came with mixed results – the Blue Oval managed to retain (slowly dwindling) interest for the Ford Mustang, which shows a tendency to regain its popularity over the past year, while GM had to pull the plug on the Camaro in December 2023, making the 2024 model year the final one so far for the iconic pony and muscle car.
Photo: Motorcar Classics While it may have lost some of its appeal among American muscle car fans, the Chevrolet Camaro remains a great option when it comes to playing with GM’s cool sports cars for anyone who thinks the C8 Chevrolet Corvette is too European after the switch to a mid-engine setup and too fixated on extreme performance with the latest ZR1 and ZR1X supercars.
So, if you want a nice-looking final model-year Chevrolet Camaro that also won’t break the bank, here’s a proposition from New York-based Motorcar Classics – a 2024 Chevrolet Camaro SS that can take its top off at a moment’s notice. The Convertible has just 4,176 original miles on the odometer, and it’s a single-owner car dressed in silver with a Jet Black leather interior.
It’s also the final model year of the iconic Camaro, and under the hood, this sixth-generation example has the classic 6.2-liter LT1 V8 engine producing an impressive 455 hp and 455 lb-ft of torque. The former owner wanted an engaging drive, and it’s fitted with the six-speed manual transmission, so you’ll have to row your own cogs – which is going to put a smile on your face if you know how to. If you don’t, get learning because it’s cool when such great cars are involved in the process.
Photo: Motorcar Classics “The interior is loaded with modern features and driver-focused amenities, while the power convertible top lets you enjoy open-air V8 performance at a moment's notice,” says the description, and it also has a spotless one-owner Carfax “report showing no accidents or damage and a documented history of regular dealership service.” As such, the car also has remaining factory warranty coverage, and it was also “superbly maintained and mechanically turnkey,” so it’s ready to make new memories on the spot.
Naturally, the dealership won’t give it away for free and instead asks for $52,500, or you can negotiate via the ‘make an offer’ tab in the online listing. So, what do you think? Yay or nay?
By the way, if you want some alternatives for around $50k, you clearly can’t have a C8 Chevy Corvette from new since the 2027 Stingray coupe retails from $71,300 with the new 6.7-liter V8 packing 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque. You would lose the opening top or pay more for the convertible, as well as the rear seats. Alternatively, you could break your vows and switch sides to the Blue Oval team and buy a brand-new S650 Ford Mustang .
Photo: Motorcar Classics The latter starts from around $33k for the EcoBoost Fastback, and if you want a matching Convertible, it’s going to be at least $41k – going out with the wind in your hair and no roof is pretty darn expensive these days, as it turns out. But you’re abandoning the massive 6.2-liter V8 for a smaller and turbocharged 2.3-liter EcoBoost inline-four packing 315 hp, a lot less than this Camaro SS. So, the best bet would be to switch to the GT version, which has the 5.0-liter Coyote V8.
Alas, while the GT Fastback starts at $49k, the Ford Mustang GT Convertible is only offered with the Premium trim level starting at over $58k – meaning that it’s more expensive than this Camaro SS. You do get at least 480 hp or 486 hp when equipped with the Active valve performance exhaust, so you have to see if the higher pony count is worth the additional cash. So, what do you think – yay or nay?
